title: Bluesky & AT Protocol OSINT Lookup Guide | MyRecon
description: Investigate public Bluesky handles, DIDs, custom domains and AT Protocol feeds via public AppView XRPC endpoints with clear source limits.
h1: Bluesky and AT Protocol OSINT: handles, DIDs and feeds
intro: Bluesky separates human-readable handles from permanent Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) under the Authenticated Transfer (AT) Protocol. Because a user can rename a handle or attach a custom domain without changing their underlying DID, MyRecon helps investigators check both public AppView XRPC responses and independent domain corroboration before connecting profiles.

sections.heading: Handles versus immutable AT Protocol DIDs
sections.body: In backend/modules/deep_search_sources.py, a Bluesky handle without a dot automatically appends .bsky.social, while custom domain handles pass through verbatim. Resolving the handle yields an immutable did:plc: or did:web: identifier, which stays fixed even if the account owner later changes their display name or public handle.

sections.heading: How public AppView XRPC resolution works
sections.body: MyRecon queries the public Bluesky AppView at public.api.bsky.app via the XRPC method app.bsky.actor.getProfile with the normalized actor parameter. After verifying case-insensitive handle equality and a valid did: prefix, Deep Search optionally calls app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed with limit=10 to inspect recent authored posts.

sections.heading: Custom domain verification as corroboration evidence
sections.body: When a Bluesky handle uses a custom domain, AT Protocol relies on DNS TXT records at _atproto.<domain> or an HTTPS file at /.well-known/atproto-did pointing to the exact DID. While deep_search_sources.py relies on the public AppView resolution, investigators can check those domain records directly as independent ownership corroboration.

sections.heading: Worked verification workflow and false-positive checks
sections.body: Start by checking whether extracted bio links in declared fields point reciprocally back to a known website or GitHub profile. Confirm each post URL on bsky.app directly in a signed-out browser, and treat reposts or same-display-name accounts as unrelated unless corroborated.

sections.heading: Honest source limits and unavailable feeds
sections.body: Public AppView queries never access private direct messages, muted lists, or accounts restricted from signed-out viewing. If getAuthorFeed hits a rate limit or timeout inside c.optional(), MyRecon preserves the confirmed profile while marking activity_available as False instead of erasing verified profile evidence.

faq.question: What happens if a Bluesky feed fails to load during lookup?
faq.answer: In deep_search_sources.py, getAuthorFeed runs inside c.optional(). If the feed endpoint times out or fails, MyRecon still returns the confirmed profile and sets activity_available to False.

faq.question: How does AT Protocol verify a custom domain handle?
faq.answer: A domain owner publishes their exact DID in a _atproto.<domain> DNS TXT record or at https://<domain>/.well-known/atproto-did. Checking those records independently corroborates the handle shown by AppView.

faq.question: Does MyRecon follow links listed in a Bluesky bio?
faq.answer: No. deep_search_sources.py extracts URLs from the profile description text into declared fields for analyst review without crawling external bio destinations.

faq.question: Can public XRPC lookups read blocked or private Bluesky data?
faq.answer: No. Queries to public.api.bsky.app only inspect publicly accessible AppView records within a 14-second deadline and 2 MB response cap, and non-200 errors remain unresolved.

takeaways: Resolve human handles to permanent did:plc or did:web identifiers
Filter author feeds by at://<did>/app.bsky.feed.post/ to exclude reposts
Corroborate custom domain handles via _atproto DNS TXT or .well-known checks
